governance.note: Inherits the caiso-30 ct-baseline lever set verbatim (CAMPD net-load-filtered outage windows, EIA-860 cogen-flagged BTM CHP host steam in btm.parquet, F923 per-plant delivered gas + measured monthly hub-spot overlay, measured EIA-930 priced interchange / per-hub intertie / gas-coupled DSW tranches, measured EIA-930 monthly hydro budget, RA must-offer midday gas floor at the measured EIA-930 NG:NG profile at frac 0.80, Argus coal-cogen BTM steam-following holdout, CT_PEAKER temperature hot-limb reliability floor + year-round local-RA baseline caiso_ct_floor_base=0.049). One new lever, tracing to a measured physical input: a POWER-ONLY heat-rate correction for the three big Kern-County enhanced-oil-recovery (EOR) topping cogens -- Kern River (10496), Sycamore (50134), Midway Sunset (52169) -- in fleet._correct_caiso_eor_power_hr (CAISO_EOR_TOPPING_FACTOR=1.8). These units report a steam-credited (artificially efficient ~5-6 MMBtu/MWh) EIA-923 plant heat rate because the EOR injection-steam fuel is credited out of the electrical heat rate, so the model priced them as cheap baseload and ran the three flat at ~88% CF (3.7 TWh in 2024) versus their measured ~0.8 TWh (EIA-923 CF 0.05-0.14, declining). The correction charges all fuel to electricity (power-only / topping-cycle basis, ~1.8x the steam-credited blend = the steam-credit ratio), landing them at ~9-11 MMBtu/MWh, the CT_PEAKER simple-cycle band where their power island physically sits, so they clear on price like a peaker. This is forward-derivable turbine physics that responds to changed gas/steam conditions (admissible under CLAUDE.md #11/#12, the same measured-physics HR correction as MIXED_FACILITY_STEAM_HR), applied to the three named plants only and NOT tuned to a TWh residual: the multiplier is the steam-credit ratio, the offer curve for the rest of CT_CHP is unchanged. See docs/caiso-eor-power-hr-2026-06.md.
governance.improvement_note: Structural fix to the C1 CT_CHP fuel-mix class, which was FAILING in the caiso-30 keeper (model 6.95 vs actual 3.49 TWh in 2024, +3.46, outside the +-2.18 band -- the prior handoff's 'CT_CHP PASS' was an eyeballed mislabel; the verdict scores it FAIL). The EOR power-only HR correction brings CT_CHP into band in EVERY scored year: 2023 3.36 vs 3.47 (-0.11 PASS), 2024 3.54 vs 3.49 (+0.05 PASS), 2025 3.72 vs 2.78 (+0.94 PASS). Determination stays NOT-YET: CC_REGULAR REGRESSES (+5.45/+5.44 vs the caiso-30 +2.33/+3.44) and CT_PEAKER stays under (-2.45/-2.28). This is diagnostic, not a defeat of the fix: the EOR over-dispatch was MASKING a ~+5 TWh domestic-gas-over / import-under imbalance; removing the EOR phantom relocates the same surplus from CT_CHP onto CC_REGULAR (the next-cheapest domestic gas) rather than onto imports, because the model under-imports / over-exports in the evening ramp (hours 16-21; h18 net import ~0.85 GW, with ~2 GW of uneconomic evening export on the priced bidirectional corridors). The prior handoff's proposed C1 unlock -- netting the CHP/EOR steam-following gas out of the midday gas-floor target and scoping the floor to the flexible CC+CT_PEAKER fleet -- was IMPLEMENTED and REJECTED this session: it made CC_REGULAR worse (59.3/60.5 TWh), because the CHP steam floors are ~0 in the artifact so the netting subtracts nothing and the scoping merely shifts the midday target onto CC_REGULAR; the gas floor is not the binding constraint midday (model midday gas 21.3 > floor 19.2 TWh). The remaining C1 closure (CC_REGULAR over, CT_PEAKER under) is therefore coupled to C3 (LMP +47-69%, 616 h>$200 scarcity tail) through the EVENING-RAMP IMPORT REPRESENTATION, not the gas floor: the per-hub bidirectional corridors permitting uneconomic evening export and the corridor ATC / import-tranche pricing in hours 16-21. That is the next session's target; the EOR power-only HR correction is the structurally-correct merit fix that stays in (CLAUDE.md #1/#11) and sharpens the residual onto the import/corridor representation rather than burying it in a mispriced cogen. C3 LMP level and C2/C5 are otherwise unchanged from caiso-30.
